current_stage.plan_excerpt:
### S0. Kernel shell, tile mapping, and resource reservation

Implement one CTA per token with `224` threads and fixed tile shapes `QK=(64,32,16)` and `PV=(64,128,16)`. The kernel owns no runtime workspace, but it does opt into about `154 KiB` of dynamic SMEM and reserves `512` TMEM columns because the live `tS + tO` footprint rounds up to the full Blackwell allocation quantum. W3 owns the `TmemAllocator` lifetime through a named barrier, and validation mode exports launch metadata so `run_stage_validation` can check block size, grid mapping, SMEM bytes, and TMEM column count before any math is turned on.

stage_result.frontier_validation_report: run_stage_validation(S0, kernel_0.py::validate_stage__s0_shell) completed with exit code 0 but 0/5 synthetic cases passed. Failed cases: num_tokens=1,2,6,7,8.
stage_result.message: Implemented the S0 shell/config/resource scaffolding and validation harness updates in solution/dsa_attention/kernel_0.py, but the S0 frontier still fails the synthetic validator in all 5 cases.
stage_result.reflection: I tightened the stage-0 slice around the payload contract: added scalar-tensor sm_scale normalization for validator inputs, kept the one-CTA-per-token KernelConfig constants, added a CuTe @cute.jit host launcher with explicit grid/block/SMEM launch parameters, corrected the shell SMEM allocator accounting for the shared-storage header, and routed validate_stage__s0_shell through the forward shell path before checking the eager S0 metadata reference. Despite that, the canonical frontier check still reports 0/5 passes with no surfaced per-case diff, so the remaining blocker appears to be the hidden validator-facing ABI for S0 debug export comparison/return layout rather than the basic resource constants themselves. The smallest next fix is to align validate_stage__s0_shell and the exported debug tensors/globals to the exact bench_synthetic contract while preserving the current shell launcher and resource reservation structure. Regression risk is low because there were no previously approved prefixes and the edits remain confined to kernel_0.py.

kernel_contract.summary: Single-kernel, one-CTA-per-token Deepseek sparse attention forward for the fixed h16 / ckv512 / kpe64 / topk2048 / page64 decode shape on Blackwell sm100a.

items.value: `kernel_0.py` will expose a single forward kernel entry point for sparse attention decode plus validation helpers named `validate_stage__s0_shell` through `validate_stage__s5_epilogue`.
Grid is `(num_tokens, 1, 1)` and block is `(224, 1, 1)` = 7 warps, with one CTA assigned to one token across all 16 query heads.

Inputs are `q_nope[num_tokens,16,512]`, `q_pe[num_tokens,16,64]`, `ckv_cache[num_pages,64,512]`, `kpe_cache[num_pages,64,64]`, `sparse_indices[num_tokens,2048]`, and scalar `sm_scale`; `-1` indices are invalid and must be zero-masked.
Outputs are `out[num_tokens,16,512]` in bf16 and `lse[num_tokens,16]` in fp32 base-2 units, matching the eager baseline semantics exactly.
No runtime workspace is required in the fast path; validation mode adds optional GMEM debug export surfaces only.
The kernel opts into about 154 KiB dynamic SMEM per CTA and reserves 512 TMEM columns, making the design intentionally 1 CTA/SM on B200.
The kernel uses padded MMA row extent `M_pad = 64`, QK tile `(64,32,16)`, and PV tile `(64,128,16)`; only rows `0:16` are semantically live and rows `16:64` are zero-filled.

resource_ledger.summary: Frozen round-0 resource plan: 7 warp-specialized warps, ~154 KiB SMEM, 512 TMEM columns, staged sparse gather, and single-CTA occupancy.

items.value: W0=index/TMA, W1-W2=sparse gather, W3=QK+PV MMA, W4-W5=softmax, W6=correction+epilogue.
Target caps are W0=32 regs/thread, W1-W2=96, W3=224, W4-W5=192, W6=128 using `setmaxregister_decrease()` / `setmaxregister_increase()` after warp-role dispatch.
Dynamic SMEM budget is about 154 KiB: double-buffered `sKc_qk`, `sV_pv`, `sKp`, index buffers, Q phase buffers, `sP`, output staging, and barrier/descriptor scratch.
Live TMEM payload is `tS[64,32]` fp32 (~8 KiB) plus `tO[4][64,128]` fp32 (~128 KiB), which rounds to 512 TMEM columns because allocation must be a power of two in 32-column quanta.
TMEM is the hard limiter, so the kernel is frozen at 1 CTA/SM; this is acceptable because the CTA streams 64 sparse tiles per token with deep intra-CTA overlap.
P0 sparse-index TMA depth=2, P1 sparse gather depth=2, P2 logits-to-softmax depth=1, P3 softmax-to-PV depth=1.
Each of P0-P3 has its own mbarrier array; TMEM allocation uses a named barrier shared across participating warps; no cluster barriers or multicast barriers are used.
Q is not kept resident in TMEM; W3 reloads 64x16 padded Q slices from GMEM into a small SMEM A-buffer so the scarce TMEM budget stays focused on logits and output accumulators.

async_pipelines.name: Sparse-index TMA pipeline
async_pipelines.payload: Contiguous 32-element sparse index tile for one token staged into `sIdx[2]` before irregular gather.
async_pipelines.smem_budget: `sIdx[2][32]` plus mbarrier state, about 512 B total.
async_pipelines.register_budget: W0 at 32 regs/thread; W1-W2 at 96 regs/thread while consuming the index tile.

async_pipelines.name: Sparse gather to QK/PV pipeline
async_pipelines.payload: Double-buffered `sKc_qk`, `sV_pv`, `sKp`, and valid-mask state for one sparse tile.
async_pipelines.smem_budget: Per stage about 68 KiB (`32 KiB sKc_qk + 32 KiB sV_pv + 4 KiB sKp + mask`), about 136 KiB double-buffered.
async_pipelines.register_budget: W1-W2 at 96 regs/thread; W3 at 224 regs/thread.

async_pipelines.name: QK UMMA to softmax pipeline
async_pipelines.payload: Single live TMEM logits tile `tS[64,32]` with a readiness handoff to the softmax/correction warps.
async_pipelines.smem_budget: Barrier state plus row-stat scratch only; no large staged SMEM tensor is added by the pipeline itself.
async_pipelines.register_budget: W3 at 224 regs/thread; W4-W5 at 192 regs/thread; W6 at 128 regs/thread.

async_pipelines.name: Softmax and correction to PV pipeline
async_pipelines.payload: Normalized probability tile `sP[64,32]` plus the sequencing point that guarantees corrected `tO` is visible before PV MMAs issue.
async_pipelines.tmem_budget: `tO` remains live in place at about 128 KiB; the pipeline sequences access rather than allocating another TMEM buffer.
async_pipelines.register_budget: W4-W5 at 192 regs/thread; W6 at 128 regs/thread; W3 at 224 regs/thread.

stages.title: Sparse-index TMA and irregular KV/KPE gather
stages.description: Implement P0 and P1 so the CTA can TMA-stage index tiles, decode page/slot pairs, gather sparse K/V/KPE rows, and derive both the QK-facing and PV-facing CKV layouts.
outputs: Tile-0 sparse indices and valid mask.
Tile-0 gathered CKV/KPE tensors and PV-facing CKV view.
checks: All S0 checks still pass, and `debug_s1_indices_tile0` / `debug_s1_valid_mask_tile0` match the eager baseline decode of sparse positions `0:32` including `-1` invalid handling.

`debug_s1_ckv_tile0`, `debug_s1_kpe_tile0`, and `debug_s1_v_tile0` match the eager gathered tensors for tile 0, with invalid lanes zero-filled and the PV view equal to a pure layout transform of canonical CKV staging.
stages.plan_excerpt:
### S1. Sparse-index TMA and irregular KV/KPE gather

Wire P0 and P1. W0 TMA-loads `32` sparse indices per stage into `sIdx[2]`. W1-W2 decode page/slot, build the tile valid mask, gather `ckv_cache` once into `sKc_qk[2]`, gather `kpe_cache` into `sKp[2]`, and then derive the pv-friendly `sV_pv[2]` view from the canonical `sKc_qk[2]` buffer with an SMEM layout transform. Invalid indices are zero-filled in every gathered tensor and cleared in the valid mask.

stages.title: QK tcgen05 mainloop into TMEM logits
stages.description: Use W3 to stream padded Q slices through tcgen05 BF16 MMAs against the gathered CKV and KPE tiles, producing raw fp32 logits in TMEM.
outputs: Tile-0 raw fp32 logits in TMEM materialized to GMEM for validation.
Verified QK accumulator shell for live rows `0:16` and sparse columns `0:32`.
checks: All S0-S1 checks still pass, and `debug_s2_logits_tile0` matches the eager fp32 raw QK logits for heads `0:16` and sparse positions `0:32` before scaling by `sm_scale`.
Rows `16:64` are provably zero-padded and therefore never contaminate the live `0:16` logits checked by the validator.
stages.plan_excerpt:
### S2. QK tcgen05 mainloop into TMEM logits

Implement the W3 QK mainloop over the current sparse tile. For each `K=16` slice of `q_nope` and `q_pe`, W3 loads a small padded `64 x 16` A-buffer, zero-fills rows `16:64`, and issues tcgen05 BF16 MMA against `sKc_qk` and `sKp`. The result is a raw fp32 logits tile `tS[64,32]` in TMEM; only rows `0:16` are later observed.

stages.title: Streaming softmax, online correction, and P materialization
stages.description: Consume the TMEM logits tile with W4-W6, update streaming base-2 softmax state, rescale existing output accumulators when the row max changes, and materialize normalized P into SMEM.
outputs: Tile-0 row max, row sum, and alpha correction factors in base-2 form.
Tile-0 normalized probability tile `P` materialized in SMEM layout and exported in validation mode.
checks: All S0-S2 checks still pass, and `debug_s3_row_max_tile0` / `debug_s3_row_sum_tile0` equal the eager online softmax state after processing sparse tile 0 in base-2 units.
`debug_s3_alpha_tile0` matches `exp2(m_old - m_new)`, and `debug_s3_p_tile0` matches the eager normalized probabilities for heads `0:16`, sparse positions `0:32`, with padded rows forced to zero.
stages.plan_excerpt:
### S3. Streaming softmax, online correction, and P materialization

Wire P2 and P3. W4-W5 load `tS` from TMEM, multiply by `sm_scale * log2(e)`, apply the tile valid mask, and update running `row_max_base2` and `row_sum_base2` for the 16 live heads. W6 computes the correction factor `alpha = exp2(m_old - m_new)` and rescales the TMEM output accumulators before PV. W4-W5 then materialize the normalized `P` tile into `sP[64,32]` in bf16, with padded rows forced to zero.

stages.title: PV tcgen05 accumulation into TMEM output
stages.description: Have W3 consume `sP` and `sV_pv` after the P3 handoff and accumulate the four 128-wide PV slices into the final fp32 TMEM output accumulator.
outputs: Final fp32 TMEM output accumulator materialized to GMEM in validation mode.
Final fp32 base-2 LSE values after the full sparse stream.
checks: All S0-S3 checks still pass, and `debug_s4_o_accum_fp32` matches the eager float attention output before bf16 conversion across all 16 heads and 512 output channels.
`debug_s4_lse_base2_fp32` matches the eager final base-2 LSE after all 64 sparse tiles have contributed, including the all-invalid `-inf` path when `row_sum_base2 == 0`.
stages.plan_excerpt:
### S4. PV tcgen05 accumulation into TMEM output

After P3 commits, W3 consumes `sP` and `sV_pv` and issues four PV MMA slices of width `128`, accumulating into `tO[4][64,128]` in fp32. The gather stage is released only after the PV updates for the tile complete, so the double-buffered sparse staging remains correct under overlap.

stages.title: Epilogue store and final validation frontier
stages.description: Finalize base-2 LSE, convert the fp32 accumulator to bf16, TMA-store the live `16 x 512` output, and validate the full kernel result against the eager reference.
outputs: Final bf16 output tensor export for validation mode.
Final fp32 base-2 LSE export and all-invalid sentinel observables.
checks: All S0-S4 checks still pass, and `debug_s5_out_bf16` / `debug_s5_lse_base2_fp32` match the eager PyTorch reference within final bf16/fp32 tolerances.
`debug_s5_all_invalid_mask` verifies the sentinel path: tokens with no valid sparse indices produce zero bf16 output and `-inf` fp32 base-2 LSE.
stages.plan_excerpt:
### S5. Epilogue store and validation exports

After the last sparse tile, W6 finalizes `lse = row_max_base2 + log2(row_sum_base2)` for live rows, handles the `row_sum_base2 == 0` all-invalid case, converts the four TMEM output slices to bf16, stages each live `16 x 128` tile in `sO_store`, and TMA-stores them to GMEM. Validation mode additionally exports the selected cumulative frontier tensors: launch metadata, gathered tile 0, raw logits tile 0, softmax state tile 0, final fp32 accumulator, and final fp32 base-2 LSE before checking final bf16 `out`.
